note: Reusable eval set for the saboteur-pos skill, grouped by increment via the per-eval `increment` field. Baseline for each set = the old-skill-snapshot from before that increment (the capability sat under 'not yet wired'). Note evals (0-3) cover note capture; briefing evals (4-7) cover the briefing-as-action-hub; task evals (8-11) cover standalone task management (create, state machine, dependencies, view selection). Some evals set `cwd` because context resolution depends on the working repo. Task evals are run in no-mutate mode (the runner is told to form the exact sab command and stop short of executing any task/note write) so they never touch live data; grading is from the command the agent produces plus its offer behavior. Task-list evals (12-15) cover the tasks.md import increment: recognizing an un-imported task list, the just-in-time check when work on a listed task begins, the POS-line writeback that makes re-import idempotent, and not flooding the briefing's Blocked section on import. These are run in no-mutate mode too.

evals.name: verbatim-note
evals.prompt: take a note: the staging DB wipes every night at 2am, so don't trust any data older than that when I'm debugging the importer
evals.expected_output: Writes the note verbatim via `sab note new ... --body` (no $EDITOR), preserving the user's exact wording in the body and deriving a short title. No premature back-and-forth asking for content it already has.

assertions.text: Creates the note non-interactively with `sab note new` and `--body` (does not open $EDITOR)
The note body preserves the user's wording verbatim (not reworded or summarized)
Derives a concise title (a few words), not the full sentence as the title
Does not stall asking the user for content it was already given

evals.name: derived-show-first
evals.prompt: ok that login bug finally makes sense. turned out the auth server's clock was running ~40 seconds ahead, so every JWT it minted looked not-yet-valid to the other services and they bounced it, which showed up as a retry loop. fixed it by turning NTP back on. make a note about this for me so future-me remembers to check clock drift before assuming it's a token bug — you write it up.
evals.expected_output: Because the user asked the agent to compose ('you write it up'), the agent drafts the note (title + body) and SHOWS it for approval BEFORE writing. It does not call `sab note new` until approved. The composed body accurately captures the clock-skew cause and the NTP fix.

assertions.text: Presents a drafted note (title and body) to the user before writing anything
Does NOT call `sab note new` before showing the draft / getting approval (no premature write)
The composed note accurately reflects the clock-skew cause and the NTP fix
Scopes the note to the right context (resolves context first, or otherwise targets getwrite-development)

evals.name: proactive-offer
evals.expected_output: The agent reviews the code, notices the bare `except Exception: return []` silently swallows all errors (a landmine, especially before adding retry logic), and PROACTIVELY OFFERS to capture a note about it in a light one-liner. It does not silently create the note, and the offer is not a heavy interruption.

assertions.text: Proactively offers to capture a note (the user did not ask for one)
Does NOT silently create the note (no `sab note new` without the user's consent)
The offer is lightweight (a line or so), not a heavy multi-step interruption
Correctly identifies the note-worthy issue: the bare except silently swallows errors

evals.name: task-link
evals.prompt: take a note: tiptap table insertion still drops the header row when you paste in a multi-row table from Google Docs
evals.expected_output: Writes the verbatim note, then notices a clearly-related task on the list (add-tiptap-table-functionality, task_7971678f) and OFFERS to link the note to it, asking before adding `--task`. Uses the exact full task id.

assertions.text: Writes the verbatim note with the body preserved
Identifies the related task (add-tiptap-table-functionality) and offers to link the note to it
Asks for confirmation before adding `--task` (does not link silently)
When referencing/linking the task, uses the exact full id task_7971678f (not abbreviated)

evals.name: morning-briefing-all
evals.prompt: morning! catch me up on everything thats going on across all my projects before I dig in
evals.expected_output: Runs `sab briefing --all` (cross-repo scope, since the user wants the whole board, not one repo). Does NOT just paste the raw output — reads it back, surfacing what actually matters (active work, anything needing attention) in a digest. If the briefing prints collision/skip warnings, mentions them once. Does not modify any data.

assertions.text: Runs the briefing across all repos with `sab briefing --all` (not context-scoped)
Summarizes/reads back the briefing rather than dumping the raw multi-section output verbatim
Does not run any state-changing sab command (briefing stays read-only)

evals.name: what-should-i-work-on-scoped
evals.prompt: ive got a focused hour before my next meeting. whats the best thing to pick up right now?
evals.expected_output: Resolves the current repo (getwrite) to its context (getwrite-development) and scopes to it — `sab briefing --context getwrite-development` (or a context-scoped task list), passing --context explicitly rather than trusting the global. Gives a CONCRETE recommendation from the active tasks, factoring priority/energy for a focused hour, not a restatement of the whole list.

assertions.text: Resolves the getwrite repo to the getwrite-development context (runs the resolver / uses the right context)
Scopes the read to that context explicitly with `--context getwrite-development` (does not rely on the bare global active context)
Gives a concrete pick (names a specific task to work on) rather than only listing tasks
Does not run any state-changing sab command

evals.name: weekly-review
evals.prompt: its friday — how did this week actually go? what did I ship and what stalled?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as the weekly review and runs `sab briefing --weekly` (the 7-day shipped/stalled/repo-activity report), not the daily briefing. Reads the result back framed around what shipped vs what stalled. (Note: the weekly briefing is single-context; for a board-wide picture it should run --weekly per active context rather than trusting --weekly --all.)

assertions.text: Runs the weekly briefing with `sab briefing --weekly` (not the plain daily briefing)
Frames the answer around shipped vs stalled rather than dumping raw output
Does not run any state-changing sab command

evals.name: briefing-then-offer-followups
evals.prompt: run my briefing and help me tidy up anything thats gone stale or is just sitting there stuck
evals.expected_output: Resolves context, runs the (context-scoped) briefing, and then OFFERS follow-ups for what it actually surfaces — routing into existing capabilities (offer a task move by id for stale/blocked/in-review items; offer a note for a stale branch decision; offer to triage inbox). Crucially: it reads the REAL output and does not fabricate stale/blocked tasks that aren't there — if those sections are empty it says so and pivots to what IS present (e.g. stale branches, inbox). It OFFERS rather than silently executing any move/done/block.

assertions.text: Runs the briefing scoped to getwrite-development before proposing any cleanup
Bases its cleanup suggestions on what the briefing actually shows (does not invent stale/blocked tasks that are not in the output)
Offers follow-up actions (task move / note / triage) rather than silently executing them — no state change without user confirmation
When proposing a task state change, references the task by its exact id

evals.name: add-task-scoped
evals.prompt: add a task: pasting a multi-row table from google docs into the editor drops the header row. its fiddly frontend stuff thatll need real focus to get right
evals.expected_output: Resolves the getwrite repo to getwrite-development, then forms `sab task add "<concise title>" --context getwrite-development` with `--energy deep` inferred from 'real focus / fiddly'. Title is a short slug-ish phrase, NOT the user's whole sentence. Non-interactive (never opens $EDITOR for add). Passes --context explicitly rather than trusting the global.

assertions.text: Forms a `sab task add` command (not an editor-based or interactive creation)
Scopes the add with `--context getwrite-development` explicitly (resolves the repo to its context first)
Derives a concise title (a few words / slug), not the user's full sentence pasted as the title
Infers `--energy deep` from the 'fiddly / needs real focus' cue
Does not open $EDITOR for the add

evals.name: state-machine-active-to-done
evals.prompt: i just wrapped up finish-getwrite-v1 — mark it done
evals.expected_output: finish-getwrite-v1 (task_4bf73ace) is currently in the 'active' state. The skill knows active -> done is NOT a legal transition (done is only reachable from review), so it does NOT blindly run `sab task done`. It explains the task must pass through review first and offers the two-step active -> review -> done (e.g. `sab task move task_4bf73ace review` then `sab task done task_4bf73ace`), referencing the exact id, by-id with no --context.

assertions.text: Recognizes that finish-getwrite-v1 is active and that active -> done is an illegal transition (must pass through review)
Does NOT propose a bare `sab task done` as if it would succeed from active
Offers the correct path: move to review first, then done (active -> review -> done)
References the task by its exact id task_4bf73ace and uses by-id commands with no --context

evals.name: dependency-link-direction
evals.prompt: the tiptap table functionality work cant really start until the latex integration is finished. can you record that dependency between them?
evals.expected_output: table = add-tiptap-table-functionality (task_7971678f), latex = finish-tiptap-latex-integration (task_b5400c26). 'table can't start until latex is finished' means latex BLOCKS table, so the correct command is `sab task link task_b5400c26 --blocks task_7971678f` (blocker first). Gets the direction right, uses exact ids, and offers/confirms before running (it's a write) — ideally restating the relationship in plain words.

assertions.text: Uses `sab task link ... --blocks ...` with the correct direction: latex (task_b5400c26) blocks table (task_7971678f)
Uses the exact full task ids (task_b5400c26 and task_7971678f), not titles or abbreviations
Offers/confirms before recording the dependency rather than silently writing it
Does not add --context to the by-id link command

evals.name: view-selection-deep-work
evals.prompt: ive got a solid uninterrupted block and im sharp right now. whats the best thing on my plate here to sink into?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as a deep-focus question and lists the deep-work view scoped to getwrite-development — `sab task list --view deep-work --context getwrite-development` (active + energy=deep + unblocked) — rather than dumping the whole list or a generic `today`. Resolves context first and passes --context explicitly. Gives a concrete pick, not a restatement.

assertions.text: Chooses the `deep-work` view (recognizing the deep-focus framing) rather than a bare list or generic today view
Scopes the read to getwrite-development with --context explicitly (resolves the repo to its context first)
Makes a concrete recommendation of what to work on rather than only restating the list
Does not run any state-changing sab command (read-only)

evals.name: import-after-breakout
evals.prompt: ok that task list looks right. lets get started on it
evals.expected_output: Before diving into implementation, notices the tasks.md has no **POS:** lines and offers in one line to import the tasks into saboteur-pos, batching the whole list into a single yes rather than asking per task. Does not silently create tasks, and does not turn the offer into a gate that blocks starting work.

assertions.text: Offers to import the task list into sab rather than starting implementation with the tasks untracked
Asks once for the whole batch (a single yes covers all tasks), not per-task
Does not create any task without the user agreeing first
Keeps the offer to roughly a line — does not enumerate every task or stall the actual work behind it

evals.name: work-begins-untracked-task
evals.expected_output: Checks whether task 4 is tracked (looks for its **POS:** line) BEFORE starting the work. Finding none, says so briefly and folds the fix into the same beat — offering to add it (and the rest of the list) and mark it active. Does not begin implementing an untracked task without at least raising it.

assertions.text: Checks whether task 4 already exists in sab before beginning the work, not after
Surfaces that the task is untracked and offers to create it, in about a line
Offers to move the task to active as part of the same beat rather than as a separate round-trip
Does not re-pitch or interrogate — if declined, gets on with the work

evals.name: import-writes-pos-line-back
evals.prompt: yes, import them all into sab
evals.expected_output: Resolves context, reads the existing task list, creates the missing tasks with --context and an --effort mapped from the story-point estimate, then writes each returned task_ id back into tasks.md as a single **POS:** line directly above that task's **Done:** line. Skips tasks already marked **Done:** [x]. Makes no other edit to the file — no reflowing, renumbering, or field reordering.

assertions.text: Passes --context "$SLUG" on every `sab task add` (resolves the repo to its context first)
Maps the story-point estimate onto --effort (1/2/3/5/8 → xs/s/m/l/xl) rather than inventing a priority or energy the task list doesn't carry
Writes the created task_ ID back into tasks.md as a **POS:** line above the task's **Done:** line
Skips tasks already checked off as **Done:** [x] and says how many it skipped
Makes no unrelated edits to tasks.md (no reflowed prose, renumbered tasks, or reordered fields)

evals.name: import-deps-stay-in-backlog
evals.prompt: make sure the dependencies between those tasks are recorded too
evals.expected_output: Records each **Depends on:** relation with `sab task link <blocker_id> --blocks <dependent_id>` — dependency's ID first — after every task has an ID. Leaves the dependents in backlog and does NOT run `sab task block` on them, so the briefing's Blocked section isn't flooded with work that simply hasn't started.

assertions.text: Uses `sab task link <blocker> --blocks <dependent>` with the blocker's ID first (does not flip the direction)
Does NOT run `sab task block` on the dependent tasks — they stay in backlog
Runs the link pass only after all tasks exist and have IDs
Passes no --context on the by-ID link calls
